title: Register skill — memory pointer + MEMORY.md update + cross-session smoke test
description:
Final polish and cross-session discoverability for the profile-development-rubric skill.

Why this card exists: a skill that lives only on disk in `~/.claude/skills/` is invisible to a future agent unless something reflexively points at it. Without a memory pointer + MEMORY.md index entry, the skill works in THIS session (because we just wrote it) but will be forgotten next session — defeating the whole point of building it. This card closes that loop.

The discoverability mechanism Claude Code uses: `~/.claude/projects/<project-slug>/memory/MEMORY.md` is auto-loaded into every conversation for this project directory. Adding a one-line entry there ("when working on InSpec controls, invoke the profile-development-rubric skill") + the corresponding feedback memory file makes the skill auto-discovered on every future session.

Workflow:
1. Ensure final skill version is committed at `~/.claude/skills/profile-development-rubric/SKILL.md`
2. Write `~/.claude/projects/-Users-alippold-github-mitre-amazon-linux-2-stig-ready-baseline/memory/feedback_profile_development_rubric.md` — short pointer file explaining when to invoke the skill (control review, cross-vendor adaptation, threshold pinning, etc.) and the trigger patterns to watch for
3. Add a one-line index entry to that project's MEMORY.md
4. Smoke test: spawn a fresh subagent with a control file + ask it to review. Without any prompting from me, does it discover and invoke the skill via the memory pointer?

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Final skill version committed at `~/.claude/skills/profile-development-rubric/SKILL.md`
- [ ] Memory file `feedback_profile_development_rubric.md` written in this project's memory dir, pointing future sessions at the skill — covers when to invoke + trigger patterns
- [ ] MEMORY.md updated with the new entry (one line under appropriate heading)
- [ ] Smoke test: open a new session (or simulate via fresh Agent) — does the memory pointer + skill auto-discovery work end-to-end?
- [ ] If the smoke test fails (agent doesn't reach for the skill), debug + adjust the trigger language until it does

title: Subagent cold-start validation — test skill on a fresh agent without session context
description:
Real validity test: spawn a fresh subagent (zero session context, no AL2023 history, no awareness of the delta pipeline) and give it ONLY the skill + a control + the relevant XCCDF requirement. See if the skill alone teaches it to make a defensible decision.

If a cold-start agent produces a good decision, the skill is well-encoded. If it only works because of the calling agent's session context, the skill is incomplete.

Target control: pick one we did NOT use in the self-invoke iteration. Good candidates:
- `SV-274030` (genuine no-match novel AL2023 requirement) — tests the "novel requirement" path
- One of the 11 `potentialMismatch` Tier-2 controls — tests the "soft match, needs reviewer attention" path
- A `red hat` string-match control other than 273995 — tests the "Cat 3 adaptation" path on a different example

Workflow:
1. `Agent` tool call with subagent_type=general-purpose
2. Brief the agent: only the skill + control file + XCCDF requirement excerpt + ask for the same 4 decisions (state, container/VM, adaptation, update-level)
3. Compare its output to what I (with full context) would have decided
4. Note any rubric gaps the cold-start surfaces

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Subagent invoked with ONLY skill + control file + requirement excerpt (no AL2023 board context, no delta history, no prior decisions)
- [ ] Subagent's decisions captured + compared
- [ ] Gaps identified — either skill is missing something, OR the cold-start was actually fine and skill is solid
- [ ] If gaps exist, edit skill + re-test (may take 2 rounds)

notes:
[2026-05-02] Card completed. All 3 reference skills read end-to-end:

1. `writing-skills/SKILL.md` (~650 lines) — the metaskill on how to write skills.
   Key conventions:
   - Frontmatter: `name` + `description` (max 1024 chars). Description MUST be third-person "Use when..." triggering conditions ONLY — NEVER summarize what the skill does (creates a shortcut Claude follows instead of reading the body).
   - Skills ARE TDD applied to documentation: RED (baseline behavior without skill) → GREEN (write skill, agent now complies) → REFACTOR (close rationalizations).
   - Token target: <500 words ideally, <200 for frequently-loaded skills.
   - Cross-reference other skills by name only (`**REQUIRED BACKGROUND:** Use superpowers:test-driven-development`), NOT @ paths (which force-load and burn 200k+ context).
   - Use flowcharts ONLY for non-obvious decision points / "A vs B" decisions.

2. `test-driven-development/SKILL.md` (~370 lines) — discipline-enforcing skill template.
   Has: Iron Law, RED-GREEN-REFACTOR flowchart, Good/Bad paired examples, Common Rationalizations table, Red Flags STOP list, Verification Checklist, Final Rule. Heavy rationalization-resistance machinery because TDD is enforcement.

3. `systematic-debugging/SKILL.md` (~290 lines) — also discipline-enforcing.
   Has: Iron Law, 4 numbered phases (Root Cause → Pattern → Hypothesis → Implementation), Quick Reference table at end, Common Rationalizations, Red Flags. Similar shape to TDD but with explicit phase ordering.

Decision: ours (profile-development-rubric) is methodology/Pattern+Technique, NOT discipline-enforcing. So we keep:
   - Frontmatter conventions, "When to use" triggers
   - One graphviz flowchart for the "Done" decision tree
   - Numbered phases (like systematic-debugging, since control review HAS phases)
   - Good/Bad paired examples (like TDD)
   - Quick Reference table at end
   - Worked Example near end
   - Pointers to saf-training lessons (no @ links)

We skip: Iron Law sections, Common Rationalizations tables, Red Flags STOP lists. Methodology skills don't need that apparatus.

Length target: 350-450 lines (between TDD's 370 and writing-skills' 650).

Final structure planned (will be drafted in card 95j):
1. Frontmatter (name + description, strict "Use when...")
2. Overview (one sentence + core principle)
3. When to Use (5-6 triggering scenarios + when not to)
4. The Four Phases of Control Review (Phase 1 Read STIG req, Phase 2 Read inherited body, Phase 3 Categorize w/ flowchart, Phase 4 Apply+commit)
5. State Semantics table (vanilla/hardened/N-A/attestation)
6. Container vs VM Categorization table
7. Profile Update Lifecycle table (patch/release/major)
8. Test Kitchen Quick Reference table
9. Anti-patterns (Good/Bad paired — 5-7 cases)
10. Worked Example: SV-273995 red-hat GPG case
11. Quick Reference (phases → activities → success criteria)
12. Supporting Lessons (pointers to specific saf-training/profile-development/*.md files)

Status: COMPLETED — ready to close. Next card in chain: 70i (extract rubric items from saf-training).
close_reason: Read 3 reference skills end-to-end. Takeaways + planned structure for our skill captured in notes.

title: SAF upstream PR: delta requirement-first matcher (SRG blocking + CCI tiebreak)
description:
## Description

Patch `@mitre/saf`'s `generate delta` command to replace its single-signal Fuse.js title matcher with a requirement-first record-linkage pipeline. Without this, cross-vendor STIG deltas (RHEL9 -> AL2023, Ubuntu -> RHEL, Win2019 -> Win2022 is a lucky corner case) score ~33% match rate due to vendor-prefix drift in titles pushing identical requirements into the reject band.

This card blocks our `profile-delta` (j64) work: we need a patched local saf (and ideally a merged upstream PR) before running the delta against AL2023 V1R3.

Work done to get here:
- Empirical: current saf produced 62/187 matches on AL2023 V1R3 vs RHEL9 v2.4.0 profile (33%)
- Root cause: `src/commands/generate/delta.ts` mapControls uses Fuse with `keys: ['title']`, threshold 0.3 hard-coded; 121 controls fell in the 0.3-0.4 reject band; 4 extra rejected by 1:1 dedup
- Research: Fellegi-Sunter record linkage recommends deterministic blocking on shared identifiers + probabilistic tiebreak within block (SRG-ID + CCI Jaccard + normalized title)
- Corpus survey: 300-sample of DISA STIG library confirms rule-title prefixes are corpus-derivable (dominant-prefix-before-modal heuristic with 0.5 threshold, returns "" for mixed-prefix corpora)

Branch already created: `feat/delta-requirement-first-matching` in /Users/alippold/github/mitre/saf
Hybrid delta base worktree: /Users/alippold/github/mitre/rhel9-v2r7-plus-gui (V2r7 + cherry-picked GUI/chrony feature work)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **TDD: autoDetectPrefix helper** — unit tests covering (a) RHEL9-like corpus returns "RHEL 9"; (b) corpus with leading "The " returns "The X"; (c) AIX-generic corpus returns "The system"; (d) Google-Chrome-like mixed corpus returns ""; (e) Nutanix-like mixed-subsystem corpus returns short common prefix. Tests red first, then minimal implementation.
- [ ] **TDD: normalizeTitle helper** — unit tests: strips detected prefix when present; returns title unchanged when prefix empty or not at start; handles empty title.
- [ ] **TDD: extractSrgId helper** — unit tests: returns `tags.gtitle` string; returns null when missing; handles malformed tags.
- [ ] **TDD: extractCcis helper** — unit tests: returns Set of CCI strings from `tags.cci`; returns empty Set when missing; dedups within a control.
- [ ] **TDD: cciJaccard helper** — unit tests: identical sets = 1.0; disjoint sets = 0.0; partial overlap correct fraction; both empty = 0.0 (document choice).
- [ ] **TDD: buildSrgIndex helper** — unit tests: groups old-profile controls by their SRG-ID; returns Map; empty profile returns empty Map.
- [ ] **TDD: mapControls rewrite** — Tier 1 (SRG block size 1 + CCI overlap -> deterministic accept); Tier 2 (block size > 1 -> CCI Jaccard rank, emit primary + relateds); Tier 3 (block size 0 -> Fuse fallback with `keys: ['title','tags.gtitle']` and accept threshold 0.45).
- [ ] **Integration test** with AL2023 V1R3 XCCDF + RHEL9 v2.4.0 profile fixture: assert >= 90% match rate (up from 33%).
- [ ] **Regression test**: existing RHEL7 v3r7 -> v3r8 delta fixture still produces same 4/4 match result (baseline of existing test suite).
- [ ] **Output schema**: `delta.json` includes `links` array with `{a_id, b_id, match_method, confidence, relationship, srg}` for each matched pair. Backward-compat: existing `controlMappings` field still present.
- [ ] **Local build + eval loop**: `npm run prepack` builds without errors; `./bin/run generate delta ...` with our AL2023 inputs produces >=90% match rate measured by log counts.
- [ ] **Upstream PR drafted** on `feat/delta-requirement-first-matching` branch with a PR body covering: root cause, research citations (Fellegi-Sunter, Splink blocking), corpus survey summary, before/after numbers, test additions. (Opening the PR is separate; drafting is sufficient for this card.)

## Definition of Done

- All acceptance criteria verified true with evidence in card notes (bd note <id>)
- All TDD cycles documented: test written first, failed, minimal code, passed
- No regression in existing test suite (`npm test` green)
- Before/after match-rate comparison captured as a row in `docs/delta-report.md` on the AL2023 repo when j64 runs
- Card closed only after j64 has successfully used the patched saf

## Workflow

1. `bd update <id> --claim` before starting the rewrite
2. TDD cycle per helper: RED -> GREEN -> REFACTOR, recording the log via `bd note <id>`
3. Rebuild saf locally (`npm run prepack`), point `saf` bin at the local build for testing
4. Re-run `saf generate delta` against AL2023 V1R3 XCCDF + hybrid RHEL9 V2r7+gui profile — capture new match count
5. Draft upstream PR body (URLs to research sources, corpus survey, before/after stats)
6. After all AC pass and j64 has consumed the patched output, close this card
7. **Claude-pace estimate: 90 min** — TDD cycles + build + integration test + PR draft

## Reference

- Design doc (private): `.local/specs/2026-04-20-al2023-inspec-profile-design.md` sections 2 & appendix
- saf branch: `feat/delta-requirement-first-matching` (already created, on mitre/saf checkout)
- Hybrid worktree: `/Users/alippold/github/mitre/rhel9-v2r7-plus-gui`
- Research synthesis (in-conversation, key findings):
  - Fellegi-Sunter probabilistic linkage — Splink docs
  - Blocking key + probabilistic tiebreak pattern standard in record linkage
  - TF-IDF / SBERT noted as future upgrade path; not needed for initial layered pipeline
- Blocks: `profile-delta` (j64)
notes:
SCOPE EXPANSION 2026-04-20 — two items folded into this card.

=== (A) Winston refactor (logger cleanup) ===

The existing `print*` wrappers in src/utils/oclif/cli_helper.ts do TWO jobs:
  1. Apply ANSI color via the legacy `colors` npm package
  2. Append to a module-level `processLogData` array that gets flushed
     to `CliProcessOutput.log` via `saveProcessLogData`

Problems:
- `colors` is unmaintained since 2022 ("Marak incident" — intentional DoS)
- 11 separate `print<Color>` functions is semantic noise over a color lib
- The processLogData array is module-level mutable global state

Considered chalk as replacement: rejected. chalk covers only job #1
(color). We also need job #2 (file sink). Winston is already imported
in saf and has colorized Console transport + File transport — one
library covers both jobs with zero custom abstraction layer.

Decision: replace the 11 `print*` functions + `processLogData` with a
Winston logger that has two transports:
  - Console transport with colorize() (level-based color, per the
    existing `syslogColors` scheme in src/utils/logging.ts)
  - File transport writing to CliProcessOutput.log

Scope:
- ~180 call sites across ~18 files
- cli_helper.ts (104 lines) becomes a small logger factory
- Callers switch from `printYellowGreen('label:', 'val')` to
  `logger.info('label: val')` (semantic) or a thin label/value helper
  if the label:value split needs to survive

=== (B) Tier 2 title-similarity tiebreaker fix ===

Discovered while running the existing Windows 2019 -> 2022 fixture test:
3 old controls in SRG-OS-000480-GPOS-00227 × 3 new controls in the same
SRG, all tagged CCI-000366. CCI Jaccard is 1.0 for all 9 pairs (tied).
My current Tier 2 assigns all 3 new to the first old (first-come-first-
served on ties) -> 1 primary + 2 related = match=3.

Test expects match=5 (each new maps to a distinct old by title meaning).

Fix: Tier 2 must
  - Prefer unclaimed old candidates when multiple candidates have equal
    CCI Jaccard
  - Use normalized-title Jaccard as a tiebreaker so matches land by
    content semantics (e.g. "administrative accounts must not be used"
    on both sides)

New primitive: tokenJaccard(strA, strB) -> 0..1 (TDD'd).

Revised AC: the Windows 2019 -> 2022 fixture test (the "fuzzy logic"
scenario in delta.test.ts) must produce match=5.

=== Revised estimate ===

Original 90 min -> now ~200 min Claude-pace:
  ~20 min  Tier 2 title-similarity fix + tokenJaccard helper (TDD)
  ~60-120 min  Winston refactor across saf

             inspec_profile.ts from stale @mitre/hdf-converters types —

             --noEmitOnError false, or fix them)
  ~10 min  Real-data eval (AL2023 V1R3 vs RHEL9 V2r7+gui)
  ~10 min  PR body draft

title: First vanilla EC2 eval and pin vanilla.threshold.yml
description:
## Description

Run the complete AL2023 profile against a vanilla AL2023 EC2 instance via `kitchen-ec2`, produce a `results.json`, and pin `vanilla.threshold.yml` to the observed compliance numbers. Many checks will fail on a vanilla system (that's expected and correct) — the pinned threshold becomes the floor for regression detection.

This card validates that the profile runs end-to-end on a real target: no Ruby/InSpec errors, every control produces a result (pass/fail/skip), and `inspec exec` completes within a reasonable wall time.

See design doc §3 test harness, §4 release ladder v0.5.0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bundle exec kitchen test vanilla` completes end-to-end: create → converge → verify → (optionally) destroy, without tool errors
- [ ] `results.json` produced by the verify phase, captured as an artifact (committed to `.local/` or attached to the card — not to `docs/` since it's a point-in-time snapshot)
- [ ] Summary stats documented: total controls, passed, failed, skipped, error (expect most to fail on vanilla)
- [ ] `vanilla.threshold.yml` committed — pinned to current numbers with explicit pass/fail/skip counts and a regression-protection ceiling (e.g., "failed.total.max: <current+2>")
- [ ] No `inspec exec` errors (as distinct from failed controls); every control returns a status
- [ ] `docs/vanilla-baseline-summary.md` committed with the run summary and timestamp

## Definition of Done

- All acceptance criteria verified with command output in card notes
- Threshold YAML validated by `bundle exec inspec compliance upload --no-compliance-upload --profile-path . --threshold vanilla.threshold.yml` (or equivalent) — passes against the just-captured results
- The kitchen instance is destroyed (no lingering EC2 resources)
- Card closed via `bd close <id>` after verification

## Workflow

1. `bd update <id> --claim` before starting
2. Run `bundle exec kitchen test vanilla`; capture the results.json and summary stats
3. Write `vanilla.threshold.yml` based on observed numbers; validate it parses
4. Commit threshold + summary doc; verify AC + DoD
5. `bd close <id>`
6. **Claude-pace estimate: 45 min** (includes AWS instance boot + full profile eval wall time)

## Reference

- Unit: `vanilla-eval`
- Blocked by: card `profile-cleanup` AND card `kitchen-harness`
- Blocks: card `ci`

title: Clone RHEL9 kitchen-ec2 harness to bring AL2023 vanilla box online
description:
## Description

Clone the RHEL9 baseline's `kitchen.ec2.disa.yml` pattern into this repo and point it at a vanilla Amazon Linux 2023 AMI. Goal of this card: `bundle exec kitchen create vanilla` brings up a running AL2023 EC2 instance so the team can iterate on controls via ad-hoc `kitchen login` + `inspec exec` while the cleanup epic runs in parallel.

See design doc §3 test harness. Uses `t2.small` (~$0.023/hr) and `SAF_PIPELINE_SUBNET` env var, mirroring the RHEL9 baseline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `kitchen.yml` committed — default driver (ec2), verifier (inspec), transport (ssh), pointed at the profile in repo root
- [ ] `kitchen.ec2.yml` committed — explicit `vanilla` suite definition: owner `amazon`, AMI name pattern `al2023-ami-*-x86_64-*`, instance type `t2.small`, SSH user `ec2-user`, subnet via `ENV['SAF_PIPELINE_SUBNET']`
- [ ] `kitchen.inputs.yml` committed — minimal baseline inputs the profile needs for a kitchen eval (can start empty if none are required)
- [ ] `bundle exec kitchen list` shows a `vanilla` suite with driver `ec2` and no errors
- [ ] `bundle exec kitchen create vanilla` successfully boots an AL2023 instance (screenshot of `kitchen list` showing `Created` in card notes)
- [ ] `bundle exec kitchen login vanilla` SSH's into the instance and `cat /etc/os-release` reports `Amazon Linux 2023`
- [ ] Docs: add a one-paragraph "Local test box" section to `README.md` describing the `kitchen create vanilla` + `kitchen login` + `kitchen destroy vanilla` flow

## Definition of Done

- All acceptance criteria verified with command output captured in card notes
- Running instance destroyed via `bundle exec kitchen destroy vanilla` before closing the card (don't leave billable resources up)
- No AWS credentials committed anywhere in the repo (all via env or IAM role)
- Card closed via `bd close <id>` after verification

## Workflow

1. `bd update <id> --claim` before starting
2. Test with `kitchen create` / `kitchen login` / `kitchen destroy` cycle; confirm no residual resources
3. Verify AC + DoD, then `bd close <id>`
4. **Claude-pace estimate: 25 min** (includes one full kitchen create + destroy cycle; some wall time is AWS-bound)

## Reference

description:
## Description

Convert the **Amazon Linux 2023 STIG V1R3** XCCDF and the **RHEL9 STIG V2R7** XCCDF into HDF Baseline JSON documents using `hdf convert xccdf-benchmark to hdf`. These baselines are the inputs for the structural diff (next card) and the authoritative requirement-set snapshots for this design cycle.

Outputs are transient (`/tmp/*.baseline.json`) — not committed. A tiny helper script `scripts/build-baselines.sh` is committed so the conversion is reproducible.

See design doc: `.local/specs/2026-04-20-al2023-inspec-profile-design.md` §1 unit `baseline-extract`, §2 data flow step 1.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `/tmp/al2023-v1r3-baseline.json` produced, validates against HDF Baseline schema (`hdf validate /tmp/al2023-v1r3-baseline.json` — or `hdf info` returns clean summary)
- [ ] `/tmp/rhel9-v2r7-baseline.json` produced, validates similarly
- [ ] `scripts/build-baselines.sh` committed to repo, executable, documents both XCCDF inputs by name (not local path)
- [ ] Running `scripts/build-baselines.sh` end-to-end from a clean `/tmp/` succeeds and prints both output paths
- [ ] `hdf info` on each baseline reports correct rule counts (187 for AL2023, 446 for RHEL9)

## Definition of Done

- All acceptance criteria verified true with command output captured in the card (via `bd note`)
- Script is idempotent: running it twice in a row doesn't error
- No regressions: repo still `rubocop`/`inspec check` clean (nothing in this card touches `controls/`)
- Card closed via `bd close <id>` after verification

## Workflow

1. `bd update <id> --claim` to claim this card before starting
2. Capture intermediate output with `bd note <id> <observation>` as you go
3. On completion, verify every AC checkbox and DoD item, then `bd close <id>`
4. **Claude-pace estimate: 10 min** (wall time)

## Reference

- Unit from design doc: `baseline-extract`
- Sibling: card for `baseline-diff` (next, depends on this one)
close_reason: Superseded by approach change. Original plan: convert XCCDF -> HDF Baseline JSON -> diff at HDF level -> use diff to inform saf delta flags. Actual approach: went straight from XCCDF -> saf generate delta -M with the new requirement-first matcher (PR #7253 on mitre/saf), which embeds matching logic directly. The HDF Baseline intermediate was deliberately skipped — the matcher's tier-1 SRG-block + tier-2 CCI Jaccard + tier-3 Fuse-fallback approach replaces what hdf-diff would have produced. No HDF baseline JSON artifacts produced; not needed.

title: SAF follow-up: sweep emasser  usage, drop colors dep
description:
## Description

Follow-up to card 2u4 (saf delta PR). During the Winston migration that deleted `cli_helper.ts`, we also removed every use of the `colors` npm package from the delta/logging path. The `colors` dep is still referenced in two emasser-related files:

- `src/utils/emasser/generate_config.ts` (~8 direct `colors.yellow`/`colors.green`/`colors.dim`/`colors.cyan.bold` calls wrapping `console.log` output)
- `src/commands/emasser/configure.ts` (import only)

This card sweeps those usages so the `colors` package can be dropped from `package.json` entirely, closing out saf's migration off the unmaintained `colors` dep (notable for the Jan 2022 "Marak incident" self-sabotage).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Replace every `colors.X(...)` call in `src/utils/emasser/generate_config.ts` with either (a) a thin local wrapper that uses chalk or Winston per-line, or (b) the shared `createDeltaLogger` factory if semantic logging levels fit the call site
- [ ] Remove the `import colors from 'colors'` line from `src/commands/emasser/configure.ts`
- [ ] Remove `"colors"` from `package.json` `dependencies` (or `devDependencies`)
- [ ] `npm install` succeeds with no stale lockfile references to `colors`
- [ ] Any existing emasser tests still pass
- [ ] Manually run `saf emasser configure` (or equivalent) once to eyeball the output — colors should still render; format-breaking changes are regressions

## Definition of Done

- `grep -rE "from 'colors'|colors\." src/ --include="*.ts"` returns nothing
- `jq '.dependencies.colors, .devDependencies.colors' package.json` returns null for both
- Tests green
- Card closed after the separate PR merges upstream

## Workflow

1. `bd update <id> --claim` when starting
2. Typical approach: `chalk` (smaller, maintained) as the direct replacement. `npm install --save chalk` if not already a dep.
3. TDD where sensible — emasser's interactive output is mostly cosmetic so integration testing may be minimal.
4. Open separate upstream PR on mitre/saf (not bundled with the delta PR from card 2u4).
5. **Claude-pace estimate: 30 min**

## Reference

- Blocked by: card 2u4 (the delta PR must merge first so this doesn't rebase-collide)
- Related to 2u4 only by the shared `colors` dep removal goal — the algorithmic delta work is unrelated
- Saf branch for 2u4: `feat/delta-requirement-first-matching` on mitre/saf
close_reason: Migrated to saf-cli-6wv on the saf-cli board. saf CLI work, blocked by saf-cli-auj (PR #7253) on saf-cli.

title: CI pipeline: check + lint + rspec + scheduled kitchen-ec2
description:
## Description

Add a GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) that runs `inspec check` + `rubocop` + `rspec` on every PR and push to `main`, plus a scheduled (and manually-dispatchable) kitchen-ec2 vanilla run that validates against `vanilla.threshold.yml`. AWS credentials flow via OIDC federation to an IAM role — no long-lived keys in repo secrets.

See design doc §5 CI pipeline, §4 release ladder v0.6.0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.github/workflows/ci.yml` committed — job `profile-check` runs on PR + push-to-main: Ruby 3.1 setup, `bundle install`, `bundle exec rubocop`, `bundle exec inspec check .`. Target runtime <2 min.
- [ ] Job `profile-unit-spec` runs on PR: `bundle exec rspec spec/` (no-op if no tests exist yet). Target runtime <1 min.
- [ ] Job `kitchen-ec2-vanilla` runs on `schedule` (nightly cron), `workflow_dispatch`, and push to release tags: AWS OIDC auth, `bundle exec kitchen test vanilla`, threshold-validate against `vanilla.threshold.yml`, `results.json` uploaded as artifact. Fails the workflow on threshold regression. Target runtime <20 min.
- [ ] Summary PR comment posted by the scheduled job with pass/fail/skip counts (via `actions/github-script` or similar — no external Slack dependency for now)
- [ ] No AWS keys or long-lived secrets in `secrets.*`; OIDC trust relationship documented in card notes (or `docs/ci-setup.md`)
- [ ] README gains a CI status badge for the `ci.yml` workflow

## Definition of Done

- All acceptance criteria verified with a real PR run (self-merged PR is fine — just prove the workflow fires)
- A scheduled run has executed at least once successfully
- `results.json` from the scheduled run shows pass/fail matching `vanilla.threshold.yml` baseline
- Card closed via `bd close <id>` after verification

## Workflow

1. `bd update <id> --claim` before starting
2. Open a draft PR early to iterate on workflow YAML (GitHub Actions only runs in a branch)
3. Confirm OIDC trust is set up on the AWS side; document the role ARN used (no ARN in the repo itself — reference via `secrets.*`)
4. Verify AC + DoD, then `bd close <id>`
5. **Claude-pace estimate: 45 min** (some of this is GitHub Actions iteration wall time)

## Reference

- Unit: `ci`
- Blocked by: card `vanilla-eval`
- Terminal card in the v0.6.0 milestone chain

title: Codify profile-delta workflow as a Claude skill (RHEL/Debian/SLES/AMZN/Rocky pipeline)
description:
[Re-scoped 2026-04-27]

Long-term: build the full SAF Profile-Dev Toolkit as a Claude plugin combining skills, MCP server, vector DB, and RAG over the saf-training corpus + STIG library + existing MITRE InSpec profile bodies.

Vision: a developer reviewing application source code + the relevant Application Security and Development SRG can ask the agent to scaffold an InSpec profile in SAF style, with the toolkit providing methodology (skills) + retrieval (MCP+RAG over training/STIG/profile corpora) + targeted analysis tools.

PHASE 0 (NOW, separate card 95g): profile-development-rubric skill v1 — distill the rubric for per-control review work. Skill alone, no MCP, no RAG. Sufficient for AL2023 v1.3.0 ship.

THIS CARD (9fh) covers Phases 1-4 — DEFERRED until v1.3.0 ships:

Phase 1 (~1 week): vector DB + MCP server stand-up. Fork shinpr/mcp-local-rag or hannesrudolph/mcp-ragdocs. Ingest 3 saf-training courses. Validate retrieval quality on ~20 sample queries.

Phase 2 (~1 week): SRG/STIG corpus ingestion. Add cyber.mil's full SRG library + DISA STIG XCCDFs to the vector DB. The MCP can answer "for SRG-OS-X, which lessons cover it + which existing baselines have similar controls?"

Phase 3 (~1-2 weeks): source-code analysis tools. AST parsing for target apps, mapping app surface to SRG categories. The hardest phase — actually MITRE-domain-specific.

Phase 4 (ongoing): bundle as `mitre-saf` Claude plugin. Cross-tool reuse via MCP (Cursor / Continue / Claude Code / etc.). Revisit RAG vs alternative knowledge representations (knowledge graph from MCP Memory reference server) once corpus shape is clear.

When this work actually starts, it likely moves to its own dedicated board (`saf-profile-dev-toolkit`) since it's a long-running cross-version project. Filing here for visibility until then.

Reference implementations to study before Phase 1:
- shinpr/mcp-local-rag (closest fit — code/technical-docs RAG, MCP+CLI, local-first)
- hannesrudolph/mcp-ragdocs (documentation RAG)
- coleam00/mcp-crawl4ai-rag (web crawl + vector DB)
- amornpan-py-mcp-qdrant-rag (Qdrant + Ollama for fully local)
- modelcontextprotocol/servers (Anthropic's reference servers — Memory server is interesting alternative architecture)
- Vulcan (mitre's existing STIG-development tool, vulcan.mitre.org — closest existing UX to study)

Story points: sp:21 (epic-sized — must be split into Phase 1-4 cards when starting)
Estimate: deferred (multi-week, post-v1.3.0)
Priority: P4 (deferred)

Status: deferred until AL2023 v1.3.0 ships.
notes:

New approach captured in docs/cross-vendor-profile-derivation-cookbook.md (AL2023 repo). Runbook is portable markdown; migrates to mitre/saf/docs/cookbooks/ after 2u4 lands upstream. An optional Claude skill can wrap the runbook later — the runbook is the durable artifact.

Unblocked: we start populating the cookbook now, per-phase, as we execute each step of the pilot. No longer waiting for v0.5.0 release.

Acceptance-criteria update (proposed — confirm before editing the card description):
- [ ] Runbook lives at docs/cross-vendor-profile-derivation-cookbook.md (AL2023) until 2u4 lands, then moved to mitre/saf/docs/cookbooks/
- [ ] One entry per phase of the pilot (pre-flight → delta → commit → kitchen → cleanup → eval → CI → release)
- [ ] Each entry includes: the commands, the rationale, what went wrong
- [ ] Runbook is exercised on one second profile (RHEL 10 or Debian 12) before 9fh closes
- [ ] Optional: thin Claude skill wrapper that loads the runbook into context

Status: open but actively being written. Not claimed yet (still blocked on 2u4 insofar as the saf CLI changes are prerequisites for most steps).
